dedupe_keys.name: khp informatics patient flow simulator hospital patient flow teaching tool

description: The Patient Flow Simulator is a small browser-based model of a hospital in which the user manages wards and watches how patients move from the emergency department (A&E) through wards to discharge. Users set beds, resources and staff per ward, choose how resources are distributed, pick queue policies (first come first served, highest or lowest need first), and decide when to allow overflow and boarding; the simulation then reports daily waiting times, occupancy, queue lengths and delays, and draws the flow of patients as a network whose betweenness centrality shows the wards that affect most patients. The provider is the KHP Informatics group on GitHub, which built it as a healthcare management teaching tool. Coverage is a single stylised hospital, not a real site. The JavaScript code is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 licence and runs as a static web page; the latest tag is v3.0 and the last commit was in November 2018, so the tool is stale. Caveats: parameters are illustrative, there is no calibration to real data, and the tool is intended for teaching, not planning. Simulation uses: explaining how bed shortages propagate into emergency department crowding, and exploring queue and overflow rules before building a calibrated model. Related records: the SimPy and Streamlit tutorial models (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des) cover the same ground with editable Python code.
